events.title: Roman Forces Sack Jerusalem
events.description: After breaching the city's defenses, a Roman army under the future emperor Titus secured Jerusalem and plundered it. This brought the long siege of the city to a close.
events.significance: The fall of Jerusalem was a turning point in Jewish history and in the wider Roman world. It marked the end of the Jewish revolt's hold on the city and was followed by the destruction of the Second Temple.

events.title: Michelangelo's David Is Unveiled in Florence
events.description: Michelangelo's marble statue of the biblical hero David was unveiled to the public in Florence. The sculptor was still in his twenties.
events.significance: David became one of the most celebrated works of the Renaissance. It is still a lasting symbol of Florentine pride and of artistic mastery.

events.title: Malta's Knights Survive the Great Siege
events.description: The Knights of Malta saw the Ottoman Turkish siege of their island end after nearly four months. It had begun on May 18.
events.significance: The defense of Malta checked Ottoman expansion in the western Mediterranean. It is remembered as one of the great defensive victories in European history.

events.title: The Galveston Hurricane Strikes Texas
events.description: A powerful hurricane hit the Texas island city of Galveston and killed about 8,000 people.
events.significance: It remains the deadliest natural disaster in United States history. The city later built a seawall and raised its grade, and the storm changed how Americans prepare for hurricanes.

events.title: The Siege of Leningrad Begins
events.description: German forces cut the last land connection to Leningrad, now St. Petersburg. This began a siege that lasted about 28 months.
events.significance: More than a million civilians died, mostly from starvation. It is remembered as one of the deadliest sieges in history and a symbol of Soviet endurance.
